agents.heading: AI agents
agents.description: Pick your tool, copy one command, paste it in your terminal. That is the whole setup.

claude-code.label: Claude Code
claude-code.note: Then run /mcp inside Claude Code to sign in.

codex.label: Codex
codex.note: Codex signs in through the same OAuth flow.

cursor.label: Cursor
cursor.note: Settings, MCP, then paste into mcp.json.

chatgpt.label: ChatGPT
chatgpt.note: Open ChatGPT Plugins, select +, then Add custom MCP server. Use the MCP URL and OAuth.
chatgpt.caveat: Access depends on your workspace policy. This bisibility connection requests read-only access.

claude-desktop.label: Claude (web and desktop)
claude-desktop.note: Customize, Connectors, Add custom connector, paste the URL, then approve the sign-in.
claude-desktop.caveat: Claude exposes every tool. It asks before each write tool the first time; use Allow always only for tools you trust to run unsupervised. Research runs tools without asking, so disable write tools there.

other.label: Any MCP client
other.note: Streamable HTTP with OAuth sign-in. No key in the URL.

endpoint.heading: MCP endpoint
endpoint.description: Using a tool that is not on the list? Paste this address into it and sign in with your bisibility account.
endpoint.selfHosted: self-hosting? use your own address instead: '<your-instance>'/api/mcp
endpoint.toolScope: {readOnly} of {total} tools are marked read-only. Clients and approved scopes can restrict tool availability. Paid operations such as rank checks and backlink analysis are write tools. Stored reports and cost estimates are read-only.

apiKey.heading: API key
apiKey.description: Use this when something has to run without you, like a nightly script.{created, select, none {} other { {created}.}}
apiKey.none: No API key yet. Project admins can create one under Settings → Developers.

skills.heading: Skills
skills.description: Download available skill archives for your agent. The other tasks below are planned.
skills.footer: Download an archive and follow your agent client's instructions for installing skills.

chatgptIcon.description: Use this icon when adding bisibility as a custom MCP app.

firstChat.description: In a new chat, type @ and select bisibility. Try: "{prompt}"

prompt.withChecks: Which keywords lost positions this week?
prompt.withoutChecks: Which projects and keywords can I view?

gettingStarted.heading: How to start
gettingStarted.note: Your workspace administrator may need to allow custom MCP servers.
gettingStarted.accessDescription: This ChatGPT connection can read project and rank data. It cannot change or delete projects, manage members or create API keys.

claude.accessDescription: Claude can read data and use available write tools, within the scopes you approve and your existing project permissions.

developerMode.title: 1. Open connectors
developerMode.description: In Claude, open Settings → Connectors and select Add custom connector.

addApp.title: 2. Add bisibility
addApp.description: Name it bisibility and paste the MCP URL below. Add the connector, then select Connect and sign in to bisibility to review access.

firstChat.description: In a new chat, open the + menu, choose Connectors and enable bisibility. Try: "{prompt}"

claude.note: Your workspace administrator may need to add or enable custom connectors.
